learn.title: Semi-structured data: Azure Cosmos DB and Table storage
objectives: Choose the right Azure Cosmos DB API (NoSQL, MongoDB RU, Cassandra, Gremlin, Table) or a related service such as Azure DocumentDB or Azure Table Storage
Pick a consistency level by weighing read freshness, latency, availability, RPO and RU cost
Design partition keys that spread storage and throughput and match the main query pattern
Choose manual, autoscale or serverless throughput, and database-level or container-level throughput, to minimise cost
Use global distribution, multi-region writes, TTL, change feed and Fabric mirroring correctly in a design
concepts: Request unit (RU)
The normalised cost of a database operation (CPU, memory, IO). A point read of a 1 KB item costs about 1 RU. Strong and bounded staleness reads cost twice as much as weaker levels.
Logical partition
All items with the same partition key value. Limit 20 GB of storage and 10,000 RU/s. The partition key cannot be changed after the container is created.
Hierarchical partition keys
Up to three levels of keys (for example tenantId, then userId) so one first-level value can grow beyond 20 GB and queries can still target a subset of partitions.
Session consistency
The default. Read-your-writes and write-follows-reads within one client session, using partition-bound session tokens, with latency and throughput close to eventual.
Bounded staleness
Reads lag writes by at most K versions or T time. Minimum in multi-region accounts is 100,000 writes or 300 seconds. Best with a single write region.
Strong consistency
Linearizable reads. Not allowed with multiple write regions. Write latency in multi-region accounts grows with round-trip time between the farthest regions. RPO 0 with a single write region.
Autoscale throughput
Scales between 10% of Tmax and Tmax, billed hourly for the highest RU/s reached, at 1.5x the manual rate in single-write-region accounts. Usually cheaper if average use is under 66%.
Serverless
Pay per RU consumed plus storage, no minimum. Single region only, no shared-throughput databases, up to 5,000 RU/s per physical partition. Good for dev/test and spiky, low-volume apps.
Time to live (TTL)
Seconds since last modification. Needs DefaultTimeToLive set on the container (-1 means no default expiry); an item ttl overrides it. Deletes run in the background using leftover RUs.
Change feed

Ordered (per partition key) record of inserts and updates. Latest version mode is on by default and skips deletes; all versions and deletes mode needs continuous backup. Read via Azure Functions trigger, change feed processor, pull model or Spark.
Azure DocumentDB

The new name of vCore-based Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB. Cluster (vCore and storage) pricing, high MongoDB compatibility and built-in vector search. A different service from Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU).
Cosmos DB mirroring for Microsoft Fabric
The zero-ETL way to run analytics over Cosmos DB data now. Synapse Link and its analytical store are not supported for new projects.
comparisons: Azure Table Storage vs Cosmos DB for Table

Same data model and the same Azure.Data.Tables SDK. Table Storage is cheap and consumption-based, indexes only PartitionKey and RowKey, and has no latency SLA. Cosmos DB for Table adds automatic indexing of all properties, global distribution, five consistency levels and SLA-backed single-digit ms latency.

Manual: steady, predictable load used over about 66% of hours. Autoscale: variable load, or any multi-region-write account with more than one region (same rate as manual there). Serverless: intermittent, low-volume, single-region workloads.
Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU) vs Azure DocumentDB

RU: serverless, autoscale, turnkey multi-region writes and the Cosmos DB SLAs. DocumentDB: vCore clusters for lift-and-shift MongoDB with complex aggregations, high compatibility and integrated vector search.
Cosmos DB for Apache Cassandra vs Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra

Cosmos DB for Cassandra is serverless-style PaaS with RU throughput and no cluster to manage. Managed Instance gives real Cassandra clusters with configuration control and hybrid rings with on-premises data centres.
Cosmos DB for NoSQL vs JSON in Azure SQL Database

Cosmos DB for flexible-schema documents at global scale with millisecond latency. Azure SQL JSON functions when the documents live beside relational data that needs joins and ACID transactions in one database.
Shared database throughput vs dedicated container throughput
Shared: many small containers share one pool of RU/s cheaply, but a busy container can starve the others. Dedicated: a container that needs guaranteed, isolated throughput.
traps: Strong consistency is not available on accounts with multiple write regions; do not pair them in an answer.
Serverless accounts are single region; any requirement for a second region rules serverless out.
Latest version change feed does not include deletes; use a soft-delete flag with TTL or all versions and deletes mode.
An item-level ttl does nothing unless DefaultTimeToLive is set on the container.
Synapse Link for Cosmos DB is not for new projects; choose Cosmos DB mirroring for Microsoft Fabric. Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL is on a retirement path too.
Unique keys are enforced only within a logical partition, and the partition key cannot be changed in place; migrate to a new container.
revision: Consistency from strongest to weakest: strong, bounded staleness, session (default), consistent prefix, eventual.
Logical partition: 20 GB and 10,000 RU/s. Item: 2 MB. Manual minimum 400 RU/s; autoscale minimum Tmax 1,000 RU/s.
Good partition keys have high cardinality, spread writes evenly and appear in the filter of the most common queries.
Autoscale bills the highest RU/s reached each hour, never below 10% of Tmax.
Strong and bounded staleness reads cost twice the RUs of session, consistent prefix and eventual reads.
Multi-region single write region: session/consistent prefix/eventual RPO under 15 minutes; strong RPO 0.
Table Storage indexes only PartitionKey and RowKey; Cosmos DB for Table indexes every property automatically.
Change feed for the API for Table is not supported; choose the API for NoSQL if you need event-driven processing.

questions.on: Recommend a solution for storing semi-structured data
questions.q: Evaluate these statements about Azure Cosmos DB consistency. 1: Strong consistency cannot be used on an account with multiple write regions. 2: Reads at strong or bounded staleness cost about twice the RUs of session reads. 3: Session tokens are scoped to the whole account. Which statements are true?
opts: Statements 1 and 3 only
Statements 1, 2 and 3
Statements 2 and 3 only
Statements 1 and 2 only
questions.e: Session tokens are partition-bound, not account-wide. Strong and bounded staleness read from two replicas, doubling read RUs.
